questions.stem: What percentage of the Solar System's total mass does the Sun contain?
questions.explanation: The Sun contains 99.8% of the total mass of the Solar System. Its enormous gravitational pull keeps all the planets, dwarf planets, asteroids, and comets in orbit.

questions.stem: Which of the following lists the four inner (terrestrial) planets in order from the Sun?

options.text: Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter
Mars, Venus, Earth, Mercury
Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars
Mercury, Earth, Venus, Mars

questions.explanation: The four inner planets in order from the Sun are Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars. These are small, rocky (terrestrial) planets, in contrast to the outer gas giants.

options.text: The distance light travels in one year
The average distance from Earth to the Sun
The distance from Earth to the Moon
The diameter of the Solar System

questions.explanation: One astronomical unit (AU) is the average distance from Earth to the Sun, approximately 1.5 x 10^11 m (150 million km). It is used to express distances within the Solar System.

questions.stem: What is the main difference between an asteroid and a comet?

options.text: Asteroids orbit the Sun but comets do not
Asteroids are rocky objects mostly in the asteroid belt; comets are icy objects from the outer Solar System that develop tails near the Sun
Comets are larger than asteroids
Asteroids are found beyond Neptune; comets are found between Mars and Jupiter

questions.explanation: Asteroids are rocky or metallic objects found mostly in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. Comets are icy objects from the outer Solar System that develop glowing tails when their ice vaporises near the Sun.

questions.stem: How does the Sun produce its energy?

options.text: By nuclear fission of uranium
By nuclear fusion, where hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium
By chemical reactions between hydrogen and oxygen
By burning hydrogen gas like a fire

questions.explanation: The Sun produces energy by nuclear fusion in its core, where hydrogen nuclei fuse together to form helium at temperatures of about 15 million degrees Celsius. This is not burning, which is a chemical reaction.

questions.stem: Why was Pluto reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006?

options.text: Because it has no moons
Because it is too far from the Sun
Because it is too cold to be a planet
Because it has not cleared the neighbourhood around its orbit

questions.explanation: Pluto was reclassified because it has not cleared the neighbourhood around its orbit, which is one of the three criteria required by the International Astronomical Union's definition of a planet. It orbits among other Kuiper Belt objects.

questions.stem: How long does light take to travel from the Sun to Earth?

options.text: About 1 second
About 8 minutes
About 1 day
About 1 hour

questions.explanation: Light takes approximately 8.3 minutes to travel from the Sun to Earth, a distance of about 150 million km (1 AU). This gives a sense of the vast scale of even our local Solar System.
